newsitem.title: ISRAEL: FORECAST-Israel Aug CPI seen up 0.4-0.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Israel Aug CPI seen up 0.4-0.7 pct.

text.p: Israel's August consumer price index (CPI), which will be announced on Friday, will post a rise of 0.4 to 0.7 percent, economists and Treasury officials estimate.
In July the CPI rose 0.3 percent while in August 1995 it increased 1.2 percent.
Jonathan Katz, senior economist at Capital Holdings, estimated the CPI rose 0.6 percent last month.
This would bring inflation in the past 12 months to 12.3 percent against a government target of eight to 10 percent for all of 1996. In the first seven months of 1996 inflation was 7.3 percent.
Katz said a 0.6 percent rise was slightly low for the month of August. "It could be even lower if housing prices surprise us," he added.
A stronger shekel, end-of-season clothing sales and falling grain prices helped curb inflation. On the other hand, the government raised public transportation fares by 13.3 percent.
Economists at Bank Hapoalim, Israel's biggest bank, also predict an August CPI rise of 0.6 percent while the Treasury estimates a 0.7 percent increase.

The Federation of Israeli Chambers of Commerce predicted an increase of 0.4 to 0.5 percent, saying housing, fruit and vegetable prices were stable while clothing and shoe prices fell two to three percent.

Katz said he believed the central Bank of Israel would lower interest rates by 0.3 to 0.5 of a percentage point at the end of September as a result of a relatively low August CPI. The central bank's key lending rate is 15.8 percent a year.
"The monetary aggregates are very clearly coming down sharply and the major economic indicators point to a slowdown," Katz said.
Bank Hapoalim said preliminary data indicate M1 money supply grew only 0.9 percent in August after surging 4.5 percent in July.
On the other hand, the central bank would not announce a sharper rate cut because of the widening government budget deficit, Katz added.
